title: Readout choice, not model choice, determines whether pretrained genomic language models help: a pre-registered benchmark on fine-scale 16S rRNA discrimination
description:
Analysis code, pre-registered plans, derived data, figures and manuscript materials for a benchmark comparing four pretrained genomic language models (DNABERT-2, DNABERT-S, HyenaDNA, Nucleotide Transformer v2) against k-mer counting on target-versus-neighbour discrimination within single 16S rRNA hypervariable regions.

Across 58 analysable bacterial groups in three experiments, the two approaches were statistically equivalent on a locked confirmatory test set (mean difference -0.21 percentage points, 95% CI -0.60 to +0.16; paired-t TOST against a prespecified 1-point margin, p = 4.1e-4). Two controls bound the interpretation: a random projection of k-mer counts matched every learned representation, while permuting labels reduced every method to chance. Among readouts measured on a common endpoint, moving from nearest-reference assignment to a linear probe changed accuracy about four times more than the choice of model.

The repository preserves the full analysis history, including analysis plans and panel definitions committed before the corresponding data were retrieved. Commit timestamps are author-recorded and were not independently certified before this deposit; see supplementary document S10 for what the history does and does not establish.
